items.evidence: The named unit test passes. It opens through count() (expects 1) and then reads the raw settings record with get(SETTINGS_KEY) in a separate connection, using toEqual on the five defaults, version 5 and the old records. Holdout: a v3 DB opened through openHandStore().count() and read raw gives v5 with the default record and unchanged hands, sessions and reports. A v4+ DB with changed settings is not re-seeded.

The named unit test passes: UpgradeBlockedError instance, name 'UpgradeBlockedError', blocker still at v4. J-1-01 is resolved. Holdout with fake-indexeddb: the blocker is never closed and 6 retries are spaced 300 ms apart, alternating count() and readSettings(). Call 1 rejects in 0 ms and calls 2-6 reject with UpgradeBlockedError in about 100 ms each. Only one open request is ever issued while blocked. 5 concurrent retries all reject. A call made just before the blocker closes resolves 0. The 10 s probe that hung in round 1 now rejects. Real browsers (app store module loaded from the vite dev server, the blocker a raw v4 connection with no versionchange handler): in Chromium and WebKit, call 1 rejects in 0-1 ms and calls 2-6 reject in 101-103 ms each, with blocker.version still 4. Whole app in Chromium and WebKit with a v4 blocker in another tab: the menu leaves loading, Statistics shows 'Your statistics could not be loaded.', and the console logs UpgradeBlockedError.

The named unit test passes. Holdout (fake-indexeddb and real Chromium/WebKit): after the blocker closes, the same store's count() resolves 0 within 4 ms and readSettings() returns the defaults. The DB is v5 with hands|meta|reports|sessions|settings. A later open at v6 upgrades from 5 and is not blocked, so the late connection from the rejected open was closed (it is also observed closed in fake-indexeddb). A non-blocked VersionError stays sticky (A-4). After the blocker closes, a new app tab in Chromium/WebKit loads normally.
The named unit test passes. Holdout: after one count() resolves, a raw open at DB_VERSION+1 succeeds with no blocked event and oldVersion 5.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Outside SPEC-02's single-store Given, and not blocking. Setup: an old connection with no versionchange handler (v4) is open in one tab, and app tab B's open is blocked (B correctly rejects and shows its fallback states). A second app tab C opened in the same profile then stays on the loading Home menu for as long as the blocker stays open, with no error logged, in both real Chromium and WebKit. C's open request queues behind B's still-pending blocked request and gets no blocked event. When the blocker closes, new tabs load normally. This needs a pre-TASK-3.9 build left open, which the spec treats as rare.
findings.fix: Optional follow-up: an open request that gets no success, error or blocked event within a bounded time should also reject with UpgradeBlockedError, so a second app tab cannot wedge behind another tab's blocked upgrade.

summary: All 8 SPEC items pass. J-1-01 is fixed: with the blocker never closed, every later store call rejects with UpgradeBlockedError after about 100 ms. This was confirmed with fake-indexeddb and with the real store in Chromium and WebKit, and the same store recovers once the blocker closes. End to end passes on npm run dev in both browsers. Integrity PASS. One non-blocking MEDIUM (J-2-01): a second app tab opened while another tab's upgrade is blocked still waits on the loading menu until the blocker closes.
